title: An Owl Can't Move Its Eyes. So It Does This Instead

scenes.text: An owl can't move its eyes. Not even a little.
Its eyes aren't balls. They're tubes, locked into the skull like binoculars.
So to look sideways, it turns its whole head. 270 degrees.
Try that and you'd tear your neck arteries. An owl has fourteen neck bones. You have seven.
Its arteries run through holes ten times too big, so nothing gets pinched.
That's how it stares straight behind itself. Without moving its eyes. Not even a little.

description:
An owl can't move its eyes. Not even a little.
Its eyes are fixed tubes, so it rotates its head up to 270 degrees instead. Johns Hopkins scientists scanned a dozen owls and found 14 neck bones, extra-wide artery channels and backup blood vessels that stop the brain's supply from being cut off mid-turn.
Which animal has the weirdest eyes you've ever seen?
first_comment: Bonus: a red-tailed hawk can twist its head almost as far as an owl. Which animal has the weirdest eyes you've ever seen?
